t: Maximize Sum of Weights after Edge Removals
o: Remove edges from a tree so every node keeps degree ≤ k, maximizing the kept weight. Root the tree; for each node, its incident kept edges = (maybe the parent edge) + some subset of child edges. For a child v connected by weight w, keeping that edge yields w + (best value of v's subtree when v may keep at most k−1 additional edges). Collect these 'gains' per node, sort descending, and keep the top few: at most k for the root, at most k−1 for non-root nodes (the parent edge consumes one degree slot).
k: Define g[u] = max kept weight in u's subtree assuming u's parent edge is kept (so u may keep at most k−1 child edges).
Each child edge contributes gain = w + g[child]; since all weights are positive, keeping an edge never hurts, so sort gains descending and take the top min(count, budget).
Process nodes in reverse BFS/DFS order so children's g values are ready before their parent's; answer = top-k gain sum at the root.

a.n: Approach 1: Tree DP with sorted gains
a.i: One post-order pass. For node u, gains from children are w + g[v]; g[u] = sum of the top k−1 gains, and the root's answer is the sum of its top k gains. Positive weights guarantee taking the largest gains greedily is optimal within a node.
s: Build adjacency, root at 0, compute parent/order with an iterative DFS
Process nodes in reverse order: collect gains w + g[v] over children, sort descending
g[u] = sum of top k−1 gains; at the root return sum of top k gains
a.t: O(n log n) — the sort of each node's children gains dominates (total children across all nodes is n−1)
a.sp: O(n) for adjacency, order, and g

w: Key correctness points: weights are ≥ 1 so gains are always positive (never beneficial to drop an edge you're allowed to keep), and the k−1 budget for non-root nodes encodes the parent edge. Root at node 0 and beware k = 1 (then g[u] = 0 everywhere and only a star of k edges at the root survives... specifically each non-root keeps no child edges). Follow-up: if weights could be negative you'd need a proper knapsack over the number of kept edges per node.
